transcript.text: Gas oven took ages to light tonight then went WHOOMPH and now the kitchen smells really strongly of gas even though I've turned it off. Is it safe to try again?

# No, don't try again. Treat this as a possible gas leak and act now.

A strong gas smell that lingers after the oven is off isn't normal. The delayed "whoomph" means gas built up before it ignited, which points to a fault.

## Do this right now

1. Don't create any sparks or flames. Don't light anything, don't switch lights or appliances on or off, don't unplug anything, and don't use the doorbell.
2. Open doors and windows to air the place out.
3. Turn off the gas supply at the meter or emergency control valve if you know where it is and can reach it easily. The handle is usually turned so it sits crosswise to the pipe.
4. Get everyone out, including pets.
5. Call the gas emergency line once you're outside, not from inside the house:
• UK: National Gas Emergency Service, 0800 111 999 (free, 24/7)
• Ireland: Gas Networks Ireland, 1800 20 50 50
• US/Canada: your gas utility's emergency number, or 911
• Australia: your gas distributor's faults line, or 000 if urgent
• Elsewhere: your gas supplier's emergency line or local emergency services

   They'll usually send an engineer free of charge to make it safe.

## After it's made safe

Don't use the oven again until a qualified gas engineer has checked it. (In the UK, that means a Gas Safe registered engineer.) Delayed ignition usually means a faulty igniter, thermocouple, or valve, and it can get worse.

Also: if anyone was close to the oven when it went whoomph, check for burns, especially singed eyebrows, hair, or skin on the face and hands. And if anyone has a headache, dizziness, or nausea, mention it to the emergency line or get medical advice.

Are you safely outside now?

Omg ok. I'm still inside, opening the windows now. The meter box is outside by the front door, so I can get to it. I have a slight headache but that's probably just stress. Should I turn the gas off at the meter before I ring them?

# Yes, turn it off on your way out, then ring them once you're outside.

Since the meter is right by the front door, it's on your route out anyway:

1. Finish the windows quickly, but don't linger. If the smell is very strong, skip the rest and just get out.
2. Leave the house, taking anyone else and any pets with you. Leave the front door open behind you.
3. Turn the meter handle so it sits crosswise to the pipe. If it's stiff or you can't do it easily, don't struggle with it. Just move on to the call.
4. Move a little way from the house and call the emergency line (UK: 0800 111 999). Don't stand right next to the meter while you're on the phone.

## About the headache

Don't assume it's just stress. Fresh air should help, so get outside now. Tell the emergency operator you have a headache. It could be from the gas itself, or from carbon monoxide produced when the oven burned badly. If the headache gets worse, or you feel dizzy, sick, confused, or short of breath, call 999 (or your local emergency number) for medical help.

Don't go back inside until the engineer says it's safe.

Let me know once you're out.
